title: Metric system and supermarket prices tangent
summary: Price digresses about changing units and being overcharged in stores.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Now when you start changing that, Dan, it's like when you were in Vienna and you went to Copenhagen, you came up with the metric system. Now when you came to America, I know it was difficult for you to...you can adjust because I can adjust. Here's how I adjust in a store. I pay what the thing say. And that's the only adjustment you have. The guy hold up a can of corn and it said unit price eighty cents, you pay this and that and when you get over to the counter the woman will raise it up and somebody will say another price. And you don't do anything but pay it. It's the same thing unscrupulous merchants did over the years to people who went in a store to buy a coat. The

coat was twenty-nine dollars, all right. And the man say, "Okay. Your coat is twenty-nine dollars. Ten percent tax, you owe me thirty-five dollars." And you would just pay thirty-five dollars and not think. And you only owe the man two dollars and ninety cents.
